title: Proposal for Oversight of Tattoo Retailers
what_it_is: Proposal for Oversight of Tattoo Retailers

sections.label: Tattoos, gangs and regulation
sections.summary: Minister says Police see no tattoo-gang link, Ministry does not track tattoo shops, and regulating the industry may not be feasible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether there is any link between body tattoos and identification with criminal gangs; (b) how many tattoo shops have opened over the past five years; and (c) whether the Ministry will regulate the industry and impose a minimum age for any person who wants to put a tattoo on his/her body.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: There is no indication from the Police that applying body tattoos lead individuals to join gangs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Given the many valid reasons why people choose to apply body tattoos, it may not be feasible to regulate the tattoo industry.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Home Affairs also does not track the number of tattoo shops in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, the Police will continue to take a tough enforcement stance against unlawful gangs.

sections.label: Consent, family and schools
sections.summary: Passage states invasive procedures need consent under common law, and family and schools help young people find identity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: There are some repercussions and cascading effects for the students, especially in terms of schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It is not regulated per se, but under common law, if an invasive procedure were to be carried out, and some of these involve the use of tattooing machines, then there are requirements to obtain appropriate consent from a person, who is competent, to give that consent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Having said that, beyond just the common law and the Police, there is also the role of the family and the  schools in helping young people find their identity, including on issues, such as applying of body tattoos which become permanent features on the body.
